The main takeaway from our work is that

the Ca(2+), E(2)-ATPase phosphoenzyme is not a simple phosphorylated intermediate but a complex structure with conformational changes in the protein backbone, a special environment for the phosphate group, and a Tyr residue that may be involved in the mechanism of the conversion reaction.
the Ca(2+) binding site of the sarcoplamic reticulum Ca2+ pump is located in the N-terminal region of the protein and is formed by the side chains of the residues Asp351, Glu354 and Glu356.

the conversion reaction of the sarcoplamic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase is a highly cooperative process involving backbone conformational and side chain conformational changes, which are likely to involve the entire polypeptide chain.
